decisions.summary: The placer's hand-sheet path fixed (own tag and letter-spacing kept, stacks split, several names per group, leaders matched, parent frame, face widths, later ground as cover, fixed-point rewrite, text weighs ten obstacles); the three sheets seated; their ledger entries removed; pack_audit reading fixes (wrapped/quarter-turned labels as drawn, tagged caption paired with its own kind, group label gap from the glyph's edge) plus two new stricter checks (roofed-court tubs, divider gate).
decisions.why: This is the previous round's remedy carried out, verified on the tree: caption_ledger.json now holds only Hoshigaoka's entry; make test-file tests/gate/test_hand_sheet_captions.py 5 passed; seat-label reports 48/64/61 captions, 0 off seat, and WRITE=1 on scratch copies leaves each sheet byte-identical (converges). The pack_audit edits correct how a sheet is read and loosen no threshold: the wrapped/rotated reads measure the label as drawn, own-kind pairing is stricter (falls back to all structures only when untagged), edge-to-edge is the right gap for a group label under an unchanged GROUP_LABEL_MAX_FT, the posts fix reads the right rects, and the removed test_pack_audit.py tests reappear in test_pack_audit_courts.py. Text weight 10x serves 266's 'labels never over labels'. None cuts enforcement of a GM request. D9's own figures (48, 64, 61) reproduce but carry no measurement pointer or one-shot label.

decisions.summary: Where the standard finds no free seat, a caption's existing (hand) seat is kept when it covers STRICTLY less weight than the standard's least-cost pick.
decisions.why: Implied by the adopted standard's own words (266 FR-006: a free candidate MUST beat any that covers weight; FR-007: the least total weight is drawn). Measured on the tree 2026-09-27 by a spy on hand_seat_if_no_better: 15 captions (Ochiba 1, Hayakawa 6, Ubame 8) take this branch, each hand seat inside its area or within REACH of its point subject, most of them free (cost 0) where the standard's discrete candidates all covered ink. Applying the literal candidate set would put these captions on neighbors' ink the hand seat avoids, defeating the standard's purpose. The placer's search missing those seats is a defect worth recording, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: The same rule keeps the hand seat when it covers EQUAL weight ('kept when it costs no more'), described in D9 as 'the standard's least-cost rule applied to a hand sheet'.
decisions.why: The adopted standard breaks exactly this tie the other way: 266 FR-007 'the one covering the least total weight is drawn (ties to the nearer ring, then rank)', and FR-008 for area captions 'nearest the centroid'. So D9's description is not true on ties, and the tool reports 'at its standard seat' for captions the standard would move - a hand-sheet-only tie rule that is the ledger's excuse in a smaller form, and the enforcement 266 FR-013 carries from the GM's 'one placer for all labels' does not fire for them. Measured 2026-09-27 (scratch test monkeypatching the tie to return the standard's pick, current tree): 44 captions take the tie branch, 26 of them more than TOLERANCE (1 px) from the standard's seat (Ochiba 5, Hayakawa 8, Ubame 13; up to 34.6 px, Ubame 'writing'); seat() then reports 5, 6 and 11 findings. Not impossible: with ties broken per FR-007, one rewrite reaches 0 off seat and a second is identical (converges). Its cost is two pack-audit findings on scratch copies, DARK_ON_DARK_LABELS for Hayakawa 'practice ground'/'(doubles as bale yard)' and Ubame 'latrine' - fixable by weighting dark features in the index or the audit's own remedy (a light fill), which is 'more code to change', not a ground. Remedy: keep the hand seat only when strictly cheaper (cost < p.cost), re-seat the three sheets, fix the dark-on-dark findings, re-run seat-label and pack-audit, and correct D9's wording.
